page.title: Muslim Food Transparency
page.intro: BOTIA helps you understand what a food label is really saying. In its Muslim layer, BOTIA reads the declared ingredients and cross-references them with documented criteria to give you clear explanations.
page.strict_rule: BOTIA operates under a strict transparency rule: it only reads what is written, does not certify food, does not analyse the production chain, and never invents information the label does not show.

how_botia_reads.title: How BOTIA reads ingredients
how_botia_reads.intro: BOTIA classifies what it finds on the label into three visual blocks:
how_botia_reads.halal_text: The ingredient list shows no prohibited components or signs of doubtful origin. Based solely on the printed information, no conflicting elements were found.
how_botia_reads.haram_text: The label declares clearly forbidden ingredients — pork derivatives, alcohol, or blood. BOTIA flags these immediately.
how_botia_reads.mashbooh_text: The label does not allow confirming the origin or process of a relevant ingredient. This happens frequently with E-numbers that may be animal or vegetable derived, or with permitted meats where the slaughter method is not detailed.

mashbooh_importance.title: Why Mashbooh is the most important state
mashbooh_importance.text: Classifying an ingredient as Mashbooh is not an accusation or a prohibition — it is simply a signal of uncertainty. Food labels are legal documents before they are human explanations. When there is a lack of traceability in an ingredient's origin, that uncertainty becomes the main information. BOTIA makes this visible so you have the power to decide.

why_doubts.title: Why these doubts arise
why_doubts.intro: The ambiguity BOTIA detects comes from the differences between what general law requires on a label and what international Islamic standards require.
why_doubts.row1_general: Allows grouping by function without requiring animal or vegetable origin to be declared.
why_doubts.row1_halal: Requires all additives, preservatives and enzymes to come strictly from lawful sources.
why_doubts.row1_why: If BOTIA reads an additive that could be animal-derived but the label does not specify plant or synthetic origin, it is flagged as doubtful.
why_doubts.row2_halal: Requires not only that the animal is lawful, but that slaughter was performed by a Muslim invoking Allah.
why_doubts.row2_why: Since labels almost never detail the slaughter method, BOTIA cannot assume the meat meets Halal requirements.

cannot.title: What BOTIA can and cannot conclude
cannot.can_1: Read declared ingredients from the label
cannot.cannot_1: Certify Halal — it is not a guarantee seal
cannot.cannot_2: See undeclared processes such as cross-contamination
cannot.cannot_3: Replace a religious authority or certification body

sources.title: Official sources
sources.intro: BOTIA's Muslim layer is based on the following international documents:
sources.source_1: OIC/SMIIC 1:2019 — General Requirements for Halal Food
sources.source_2: Codex Alimentarius CAC/GL 24-1997 — Guidelines for use of the term Halal
sources.source_3: EU Regulation 1169/2011 — Food Information to Consumers

disclaimer: Informative content. BOTIA analyses only the ingredients declared on the label and does not replace medical, legal, religious or professional advice.
